scenes.narration: But here's the weird part. In the nineteen thirties, doctors noticed: if a finger's nerve was *damaged*... it stayed *smooth*.

scenes.narration: So water's only the trigger. Your *nerves* do the rest. They tell tiny blood vessels in your fingertips to squeeze... and the skin above *folds* in.
scenes.headline: THE *NERVE* TRICK

youtube.description:
Why do fingers wrinkle in water? It isn't soggy skin. Your nerves tell tiny blood vessels in your fingertips to squeeze, so the skin above folds into ridges. Fingers with a damaged nerve stay smooth. Those wrinkly fingers might even help you grip wet things, like treads on a tyre (scientists still argue about that part).
